evals.prompt: Here's my first go at docs/manual.md for mytool (evals/files/draft-manual.md). Turn it into a proper man page source for our pandoc build.
evals.expected_output: The manual with its sections in man-pages(7) order, options as a code-colon list, and front matter fit for a reproducible page.
expectations: The level-1 headings appear in the order NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS, EXAMPLES, all in capitals
The options are a bullet list whose every item has the shape '- `term`: description', the term in one code span followed directly by a colon; no Markdown table remains
All three options (--listen, --relay, -v/--verbose) are still documented
The file contains no em dash
The footer no longer carries a version number, and the front matter has a date: field

evals.prompt: evals/files/setup/ is the root of mytool, a Rust tool. It has a docs/manual.md now. Wire up the man page: the build, the CI check, and shipping it in the .deb. Show every file you change.
evals.expected_output: The Makefile, .gitignore, ci.yml and Cargo.toml changed so that make man builds the page, ri-ci-man checks it and cargo-deb ships it.
expectations: The Makefile sets MAN_NAME = mytool and has 'include build/man.mk', with no hand-written pandoc rule
The answer installs the man and man-lua pieces with apply --item and adds a man job calling ./.github/workflows/ri-ci-man.yml to ci.yml, listed in the needs of ci-passed
Cargo.toml's [package.metadata.deb] assets include man/mytool.1 installed to usr/share/man/man1/
The answer says make man must run before cargo deb
No generated man/mytool.1 is added to version control
